propositions: Prompt cache writes occur on every plan-review gate call and are never read across calls, because the marked prefix boundary sits after pass-specific content rather than at the byte-stable shared prefix boundary.

The shared plan-bearing prefix (stance preamble + plan text) is deliberately engineered to be byte-identical across multiple passes within one run, but the cache breakpoint is placed after each pass's suffix, yielding unique cache keys and zero cross-pass reads.
The cache ineffective diagnostic fires only when write==0 AND read==0, missing the write-every-call-never-read pattern that occurs in single-step passes, making this waste invisible to telemetry.

Moving the cache breakpoint to the end of the byte-stable shared_plan_prefix boundary (via a RunRequest.cache_prefix knob and dynamic instruction reordering) enables within-run cross-pass cache reads and same-ticket TTL re-reads.

Single-leaf-ticket plan reviews currently incur ~9.2k premium-rate cache-write tokens per run with zero reads, costing ~2.3k token-equivalent waste; relocating the breakpoint recovers ~5-6k token-equivalents per review.
